full_judgment:
Qazi Shaliuddin J: Accused-appellants Abdul Khaleque, Shava Mia, Abdul Malek, Rafiqul Islam Kazi and Shahjalal Khan have filed Criminal Appeal No. 810 of 1994 while accused Abdur Rashid has preferred Criminal Appeal No. 557 of 1994. Both the appeals are directed against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Comilla in Sessions Case No. 74 of 1992 of 29-3-94 convicting the accused-appellants under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing each of them to suffer imprisonment for life and also to pay a fine of Taka 1,000.00 in default, to suffer RI for one year more. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that on 27-6-91 at about 4-30 PM while deceased Sirajul Islam, a Habilder of 21 East Bengal Regiment (Engineering Coreps) while on leave came in front of the Tea-Stall of one Sultan Chowdhury the accused appellants with premeditation and in furtherance of their common intention confronted him. Accused Shava Mia invited Sirajul Islam to have a cup of tea in the Tea-Stall of Sultan Chowdhury but he declined. Then accused Rashid asked him why he had used filthy language and there was hot altercation between them. Rashid dragged Siraj catching the collar of his shirt and thereafter the victim Siraj was thrown into the nearby tank. Accused Shava Mia passed the order to finish Siraj. Accused Abdul Malek, Shahjalal, Abdul Khaleque and Rafiqul Islam dealt fist blows while accused Rashid dealt a knife blow. Siraj raised alarm and witnesses saw the occurrence and Siraj was taken out of the water. He became unconscious and was taken to Chandina Hospital for treatment wherein doctor declared him dead. On receiving the information police recorded a diary and came to the hospital and made inquest of the dead body. Thereafter on the following day at about 8-30 AM a First Information Report was lodged by Kazi Tazul Islam (PW 1). Police investigated into the case, examined the witnesses under section 161 CrPC, prepared a sketch map and index thereof and after due investigation submitted charge sheet against the accused appellants and others 

 3. In all 16 witnesses were examined by the prosecution in support of the charge. The defence did not examine any witness. The defence case, as it appears from the trend of the cross-examination of the prosecution witness, is that, due to litigation and enmity with the informant party, the accused appellants were implicated in this case falsely out of the previous grudge and enmity. It is further suggested that as a result of grappling deceased Sirajul Islam fell into the tank where he has been injured by a pointed bamboo hidden in water and as a result of such injury he died. The learned Additional Sessions Judge upon consideration of the evidence on record found the accused guilty of the offence of murder and accordingly sentenced each of them as aforesaid. 

 15. PW 13 Monirul Islam is the Investigating Officer, made the GD entry being GD entry number 905 dated 27-6-91, went to the hospital, saw the dead body of deceased Siraj, made inquest report of the dead body and sent the dead body to the morgue for postmortem examination. He visited the place of occurrence, prepared the sketch map and index thereof and examined the witnesses under section 161 CrPC and took over the charge for investigation into the case. 

 16. PW 14 Inspector Lutfor Rahman took over the charge from PW 13 Sub-Inspector Monirul Islam and further investigated into the case. He also re-examined some witnesses under section 161 CrPC and after perusing the record and making the investigation submitted the charge sheet. 

 19. Mr. Sirajul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused appellants Abdul Khaleque, Shava Mia, Abdul Maleque, Rafiqul Islam and Shahjalal submitted that the learned Additional Sessions Judge misread and misconstrued the evidence on record and found the complicity of the accused appellants in the crime illegally convicted them against the weight of evidence. He has submitted that the prosecution totally failed in proving the complicity of the accused appellants with the crime alleged. He further submitted that there was no common intention to kill victim Sirajul Islam and there was no evidence which could suggest that in furtherance of such common intention the accused appellants had in any way aided to commit the crime, as such, the order of conviction and sentence passed against the accused- appellants is highly illegal. He argued that from the evidence as adduced by the prosecution there appears hot exchange of words used by deceased Sirajul Islam and the accused persons and at a certain point of time accused Rashid caught hold of deceased victim Sirajul Islam by the collar of his shirt and they fell into the water of the tank. There being no allegation or material on record to show that these accused appellants had any arms or weapons in their hands and further that while they were in water prosecution allegation is that they barely inflicted fist blows on Siraj and that accused Rashid brought out a knife and struck it into the chest of deceased Sirajul Islam. This isolated act of Rashid does not in any way entangle other accused appellants with the infliction of the blows, as such, the application of section 34 of the Penal Code, namely, in furtherance of common intention to kill is totally nil as such, the order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge is wholly misconceived and the order of conviction against these accused appellants is not sustainable in law. Mr. Huq further argued that no witness has deposed before the court stating in clear language that they saw the accused Rashid inflict the knife blow and they also did not see even the knife. Even the investigating officer could not also recover the alleged knife by which accused Rashid was alleged to have inflicted the blow on the chest of Serajul Islam which resulted in his death. The investigating officer did not even try to unearth the crime weapon as such, the defence suggestion that deceased Serajul Islam might have sustained the injury by a pointed bamboo which was hidden in the water of the tank and no such injury was caused by accused Rashid. The learned Judge did not consider the defence case in its true perspective resulting in serious miscarriage of justice, as such, the accused appellants in both the appeals are entitled in law to be acquitted. 

 22. Let us now deal with the case of accused Abdur Rashid in Criminal Appeal No. 557 of 1994. The prosecution evidence as deposed by PWs 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 conclusively prove that accused Rashid had dealt the fatal blow on the chest of deceased Sirajul Islam. It is vehemently argued by the learned Advocate Mr. AKM Faiz and Mr. Sirajul Huq that there is no eye-witness as to dealing of the knife blow on the person of deceased Sirajul Islam. PW 2 Zakir Hossain has stated in his evidence that accused Hamid Kazi passed the order to finish Sirajui Islam and Rashid dealt the knife blow and deceased Sirajul Islam raised alarm. PW 3 Md. Mustafa has stated that Shava passed the order to finish Siraj and at once Rashid dealt dagger blow to Siraj. Dagger was in the hand of accused Rashid. Siraj exclaimed that the bastard Rashid has finished him. PW 4 Md. Abdul Matin also stated that on the order of Shava to finish Siraj Rashid dealt the dagger blow and Siraj cried out by saying that bastard Rashid has given him the blow." PW 5 Rapia Khatun also stated that Shava passed the order to finish Sirajul Islam and Rashid dealt the dagger blow on Siraj and she herself saw the actual dealing of knife blow on the person of Siraj. PW 6 Kazi Abdul Wahab also deposed that on the order of Shava Rashid dealt the dagger blow on the chest of Siraj and Siraj cried out by saying" that bastard Rashid has given him the blow. He also stated that he witnessed the actual dealing of blow. PW 7 Hazera Khatun stated that Rashid dealt the knife blow and Siraj cried out by saying, that bastard Rashid has given him the blow. PW 8 Kazi Abdul Wadud also corroborated the other witnesses by saying that on the order Shava Rashid dealt the fatal blow and Siraj cried out by saying that“ল ইত্যার পোলা ঘাই দিয়াছে” “PW 9 Mohammad Hossain also corroborated the other witnesses by saying that on the order of Shava Rashid dealt the dagger blow on the left side of victim Siraj and Siraj cried out by saying that “ল ইত্যার পোলা ঘাই দিয়াছে” So that evidence of these witnesses has clearly established that accused Rashid has dealt the fatal blow on the vital part of deceased Sirajul Islam which ultimately resulted in his death. Mr. Faiz argued that the facts and surrounding circumstances should be considered before finding the accused guilty of the offence under section 302 of the Penal Code. He argued that the fact of a hot altercation between the parties and of falling into the water and of grappling and giving indiscriminate fist blow as the prosecution witnesses alleged and of giving a knife blow on the chest of deceased Sirajul Islam even if conceded Exception 4 of section 300 is attracted which reads as follows: 

 Mr. Faiz argued that the operation of section 302 of the Penal Code in the instant case under the facts and circumstances could not apply at all. The learned Judge fell into serious error in finding the accused guilty of the offence under section 302 of the Penal Code and illegally recorded the conviction and sentence. It is quite clear as the facts emerge that there was hot altercation, a tussle between the parties and there was a free style assault and at a certain stage it is alleged that Rashid dealt blow by his dagger could not in any way bring the case under section 302 of the Penal Code. 

 Although the inquest is not an evidence but nevertheless at the earliest point of time it has been recorded by the Sub-Inspector of police but we do not attach any importance to the inquest report. It is true that if an injury be caused by a pointed bamboo the injury should have normally been smooth or clean and if an injury be caused by the sharp cutting weapon the injury would be even smooth and clean. Doctor's opinion that although such injury is possible by a sharp pointed bamboo but in the instant case the injury has not been caused by such pointed bamboo. We accept the view that the injury had been caused by a sharp cutting weapon like dagger as has been opined by the doctor but in considering the manner and circumstances in which such injury was caused, we are to appreciate the evidence a bit more carefully. Judging the facts in its true perspective, we find that the occurrence is not a premeditated, cool blooded act done with the set purpose of committing the crime of murder of the victim. Rather in course of tussle, hot altercation and grappling between the parties, Rashid dealt the blow by a knife. We do not know even under what circumstances Rashid had dealt such blow when he along with the victim Sirajul Islam were under water. Deceased Sirajul Islam might have resisted Rashid and in order to save himself he might have inflicted the dagger blow. It has to be borne in mind that as there was none to stop Rashid to deal repeated blows if he had the intention to kill he merely had struck one blow which eliminates the intention to kill. Therefore, the intention to kill is lacking and it is not a culpable homicide amounting to murder but is a culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Therefore, it falls within the provision of section 304 Part II of the Penal Code. Judging the facts in its true perspective, we are of the view that the learned Additional Sessions Judge has misdirected himself in finding accused Rashid guilty of the offence of committing murder. He deserves to be convicted under section 304 Part II of the Penal Code as the action is not a pre-planned and premeditated one. In that view of the matter the order of conviction passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge against accused Rashid under section 302 of the Penal Code is altered to one under section 304 Part II of the Penal Code and we sentence him to rigorous imprisonment for 6(six) years only. 

 The appeal being Criminal Appeal No. 810 of 1994 filed by accused appellants Abdul Khaleque, Shava Mia, Abdul Maleque, Rafiqul Islam and Shahjalal is allowed. The order of conviction and sentence passed against them by the Additional Sessions Judge, Comilla in Sessions Case No. 74 of 1992 on 29-3-1994 is hereby set aside. They are found not guilty of the charge levelled against them and they are acquitted of the same. Accused appellants Abdul Khaleque, Abdul Maleque, Rafiqul Islam and Shahjalal may be set at liberty forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case. Accused appellant Shava Mia is discharged from his bail bond.
